46:1: We have already explained the meaning of His saying, “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book,” so there is no need to repeat it in this topic.
46:2: His saying: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the Wise.
46:3: And His statement, And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth, God Almighty says: We did not create the heavens and the earth and bring them into being as a manufactured creation, and what is between them of the kinds of world except in truth, meaning: except to establish truth and justice in creation. And His saying, And a specified term, means: Except for a term for all of that that is known to Him, and He will destroy it when it reaches it, and will annihilate it after it had existed by His bringing it into existence. And His statement, And those who disbelieve turn away from that which they have been warned of. God Almighty says: And those who have denied the Oneness of God turn away from God’s warning to them and do not reflect and take heed.
46:4: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:Have you seen, O people, the gods and idols that you worship besides God? Show me what they created from the earth. My Lord created the entire earth, and you called it because of its creation. I did not create any gods or lords from that. So that will be an argument for you in your worship of it. For part of My argument for My worship of My God and My singling out Him as God is that He created the earth and innovated it from nothing. And His statement, Or do they have a partner in the heavens? God Almighty says: Or do your gods that you worship, O people, have a partner with God in the seven heavens, so that you will have an argument for your worship of them? For part of my argument for my singling out worship for my Lord is that He has no partner in creating them, and that He is the One who created them, without everything else besides Him. And His saying, Bring me a book from before this, God Almighty says: A book that came from God before this Qur’an that was sent down to me, that the gods and idols that you worship created something from the earth, or that they have a partner with God in the heavens, so that will be an argument for you for your worship of them, because if that is true for them, then their partnership in the blessings that you have is true, and it is obligatory for them to thank you, and they deserve service from you because that is something that no one can create except God. And his saying, or a trace of knowledge, the reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as or a trace of knowledge with an alif, meaning: bring me a remnant of knowledge. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami said that he used to read it as or a trace of knowledge meaning: or specifically from the knowledge that you were given, and you preferred it over others. The other recitation that I do not permit is or a trace of knowledge with an alif, due to the consensus of the reciters of the regions on it. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this verse. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Or bring me knowledge that your gods created something from the earth and that they have a share in the heavens through the line that you draw on the earth, for you Arabs are people of divination, augury, and soothsaying. Who said that? Bishr bin Adam told us: Abu Al-Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Safwan bin Salim, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: A line that the Arabs used to draw on the ground. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr said: meaning Ibn Ayyash: The line is divination. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: or specifically from knowledge. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: Or a special kind of knowledge. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, Or a trace of knowledge. He said: That is, a special kind of knowledge. Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith told us: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Hussein, on the authority of Qatada: Or a trace of knowledge. He said: Especially knowledge. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or knowledge that you stir up and extract. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, or a trace of knowledge, he said: A trace of something they extract by nature. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or do you influence that knowledge from someone before you? Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Or a trace of knowledge, he said: Someone who traces knowledge. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: or a clear explanation of the matter. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Or a trace of knowledge meaning clear evidence of the matter. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: with the remainder of knowledge. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr, meaning Ibn Ayyash, was asked about a trace of knowledge. He said: A remnant of knowledge. The first of the correct sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: Atharah is the remainder of knowledge, because that is what is known from the speech of the Arabs, and it is a source from the saying of the speaker: Athar something is Atharah, like Samja is Samja, and Qabaha is Qabaha, as the camel herder said: And she had a strange feeling that she ate a plant in a barren hillock. Meaning: And the one who reads: or its trace, then he made it his trace from the trace, as it was said: a layer of dust. It has been reported from some of them that he read it or traced it with a sukoon on the tha’ like rajfa and khatfa. If that is directed to what we said about it that it is a remnant of knowledge, then it is possible that that remnant is from the knowledge of writing and from knowledge that was derived from the books of the ancients, or from the special knowledge that they were influenced by. It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that regard, that he interpreted it to mean writing, we will mention it, God willing. So the interpretation of the statement then is: Bring me, O people, a book from before this book that verifies what I have asked you to verify from the evidence for your claim to what you claim for your gods, or a remnant of knowledge that leads to knowledge of the truth of what you say about that if you are truthful in your claim to it as you claim, because if the claim does not have an argument for you, it is of no use to the one making the claim.
46:5: God Almighty says: And which servant is more astray than a servant who calls upon gods other than God who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection? He says: His call will never be answered because it is a stone or wood or something similar. And His statement, And they are heedless of their invocation, meaning that the Most High says: And their gods whom they call upon are heedless of their invocations, because they do not hear, speak, or understand. What He meant by describing them as heedless is that He likens them to a person who is forgetful of what is said to him, since they do not understand anything that is said to them, just as something is said to them, just as someone who is heedless of something does not understand what he is heedless of. This is a rebuke from God to these polytheists for their bad opinion and the ugliness of their choice in their worship of someone who does not reason or understand, and for abandoning the worship of all of His blessings that they have, and the one to whom they seek help when needs and calamities befall them. It was said: the one who does not respond to Him, so mentioning the gods, which are inanimate, is embarrassing, while mentioning the sons of Adam and the one who has choice and discrimination, is embarrassing, since their worshippers had likened them to kings and princes who serve them in their service. Thus, the discussion of that was conducted in a manner that was common among them.
46:6: God Almighty says: And when the people are gathered on the Day of Resurrection for the Day of Judgment, these gods that they called upon in this world will be their enemies because they will disown them. And they were disbelievers in their worship. God Almighty says: And their gods that they worshipped in this world will be disbelievers in their worship because they will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:We did not command them to worship us, nor did we feel that they worshipped us. We disown them, O our Lord.
46:7: And His statement, And when Our clear verses are recited to them, God Almighty says: And when Our verses are recited to these polytheists among your people, meaning Our arguments that We used against them, in what We sent down of Our Book to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, clear meaning clear and luminous. Those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, God Almighty says: Those who strove to believe in the oneness of God and denied His Messenger said of the truth when it came to them from God, so He sent it down to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, This is obvious magic, meaning this Qur'an is a deception that deceives us and takes hold of the hearts of those who hear it, the work of magic. Clear, He says: It makes clear to those who contemplate it from those who hear it that it is obvious magic.
46:8: God Almighty says: Or do these polytheists from Quraysh say: Muhammad invented this Qur’an, fabricated it and fabricated it as a lie? Say to them, O Muhammad, if you fabricated it and fabricated it as a lie about God, then you have no power over me meaning you will not be able to protect me from God if He punishes me for inventing it and fabricating anything about it, and you will not be able to ward off any harm from me if He afflicts me with it. And His statement, He knows best what you say about it, means: My Lord knows best what you say among yourselves regarding this Qur’an. The ha in His statement, you say about it, is from the mention of the Qur’an. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement, You will overflow therein, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement when you are pouring forth therein, he said: You say. And His saying, That is sufficient as a witness between me and you, means: God is sufficient as a witness against me and against you regarding what you say of your denial of me in what I brought to you from God, the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, that He will not punish them for it after they repent from it.
46:9: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people from Quraysh, I am not an innovation among the messengers. Meaning: I am not the first of the messengers that God sent to His creation. There were many messengers before me who were sent to nations before you. It is said: He is an innovation in this, and an innovation in it, if he was the first in it. Among the innovations is the saying of Adi bin Zaid. I am not an exception to the incidents that befall men who have become naked after their misery and happiness. It is a beautiful saying of Al-Ahwas: I was proud and said, “Look at me. It is not out of ignorance that I have brought something new.” It means first, it is said: He is an innovation from an innovation-oriented people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, Ali told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, I am not an innovation among the messengers, meaning: I am not the first of the messengers. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, I am not an innovation among the messengers, he said: He says: I was not the first messenger sent. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, I was not an innovation among the messengers, he said: I was not the first of them. Ibn Hamid told us: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muawiyah told us on the authority of Abu Hubayrah, who said: I asked Qatada, Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers.’ He said: That is, there were messengers before me. Bishr told us, Yazid said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers,’ meaning: that there were messengers before me. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, an innovation among the messengers, he said, There were messengers before him. And His saying, And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: It refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to him: Say to the believers in you, I do not know what will be done with me or with you on the Day of Resurrection, and to what we will be destined there. They said: Then God explained to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him their state in the Hereafter, and it was said to him, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, * That God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will come after Al-Fath 48:1-2. And He said, That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally, and He may remove from them their misdeeds Al-Fath 48:5. Who said that? Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Then God revealed after this: So that God may forgive you your sins, past and future. Ibn Hamid narrated: Yahya bin Wadh narrated from Al-Hussein from Yazid from Ikrimah and Al-Hussein Al-Basri, they said: Ha Mim Al-Ahqaf said: “And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.” Then it was abrogated by the verse in Surat al-Fath 48:Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that God may forgive you. Al-Fath 1-2… the verse. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out when this verse was revealed, and he gave them the good report that he had been forgiven for his past and future sins. He said to him: “There are men from among the believers. Congratulations to you, O Prophet of God. We know what will be done with you, so what will be done with us?” Then God the Almighty revealed in Surat Al-Ahzab and said: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty (al-Ahzab 33:47) and He said: “That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and He will remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, in the sight of God, a great attainment. And He will punish the hypocrites, men and hypocrites, and the polytheists, men and polytheists, who assume [dislike of] God” (al-Fath 48:5-6)… the verse. So God explained what He will do to him and to them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Then he knew or learned from God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that what will be done with him. He said: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest * That God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will come after. al-Fath 48:1-2. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, he said: It was made clear to him that his sins, past and future, had been forgiven. Others said: Rather, it was a command from God, the Most High, to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to say it to the polytheists among his people, knowing that he did not know what would happen to him and to them in this world. Would his affair with them be that they would kill him or expel him from among them, or would they believe in him and follow him, and their affair would be to destruction, just as the nations who denied their messengers before them were destroyed, or to belief in him in what he brought them from God? Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadheeh told us: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, he said: As for the Hereafter, God forbid! He knew that he was in Paradise when he took his covenant with the messengers, but he said: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world. Will I be expelled as the prophets before me were expelled, or will I be killed as the prophets before me were killed? And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Will my nation that denied, or my nation that believed, or my nation that was pelted with stones from the sky, or that was swallowed up by a crushing earthquake? Then it was revealed to him: And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed mankind’ (al-Isra’ 17:60) meaning: I have encompassed you with the Arabs lest they kill you. So he knew that he would not be killed. Then God Almighty revealed: “It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions. And sufficient is God as Witness” (al-Tawbah 9:33) meaning: I bear witness for you against Himself that He will make your religion prevail over all religions. Then He said to him about his nation: And God would not punish them while you are among them, and God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. (al-Anfal 8:33) So God informed him what He would do to him and what He would do to his nation. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: I do not know what is required of me and you, or what ruling will be revealed. It does not mean I do not know what will be done to me or to you tomorrow in the afterlife of God’s reward for those who obey Him and His punishment for those who deny Him. Others said: He was only ordered to say this regarding a matter that he was awaiting from God Almighty, other than reward and punishment. The most correct of the sayings on this matter and the most similar to what is indicated by the explanation is the saying of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, which was narrated by Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali. We said this because it is more correct because the address from the beginning of this surah to this verse, and the report, is an address from God, the Exalted, to the polytheists and report about them, and a rebuke to them, and an argument from God, the Exalted, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against them. If that is the case, then it is known that this verse also has the same path as what preceded and followed it in that it is an argument against them and a rebuke to them or report about them. If that is the case, then it is impossible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be told, “Say to the polytheists, ‘I do not know what will be done with me or with you in the Hereafter,’ while the verses of the Book of God, the Exalted, in His revelation and His sending down to him, are consecutive, stating that the polytheists will be in the Fire eternally and the believers will be in Paradise enjoying themselves. With this, He terrifies them at one time and encourages them at another. If He had said that to them, they would have said, ‘Then why should we follow you when you do not know what state you will be in tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection, to humiliation and tranquility, or to hardship and torment?’ Our following you, if we follow you and believe in what you call us to, is out of a desire for the blessing and honor that will be our portion, or out of fear of the punishment and torment that we will flee from. But that is as Al-Hasan said. Then God explained to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what He would do to him and to those among his people and others who denied what he brought. And His statement, “I only follow what is revealed to me,” means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: Say to them, I only follow what I command you to do, and what I do, except the revelation of God that He reveals to me. “And I am only a clear warner,” meaning: And I am only a clear warner to you, warning you of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him. “Clear,” meaning: He has made His warning clear to you, and made clear to you His call to what is in it for your advice. He says: And so am I.
46:10: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who say about this Qur’an when it came to them, This is obvious magic. “Have you considered, O people, if this Qur’an is from God, He sent it down to me, and you disbelieved in it?” He says: And you denied it. And his statement, And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it, meaning the like of the Qur’an. They said: And the like of the Qur’an to which Moses bore witness to the truthfulness of the Torah. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, regarding this verse: And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar to it. So the disbelievers among the people of Mecca disputed over it. The Torah is like the Qur’an, and Moses is like Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Abd al-A’la narrated: Dawud was asked about the verse, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God and you disbelieve in it?’… The verse. Dawud said, ‘Amir said, Masruq said: By God, it was not revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam. It was only revealed in Mecca, and Abdullah did not convert to Islam except in Medina. But it was a dispute that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, argued with his people about. He said: So the verse, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God and you disbelieve in it and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it and believes while you are arrogant’ was revealed. He said: So the Torah is like the Qur’an and Moses is like Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So they believed in the Torah and their Messenger, and you disbelieved. Abu Kurayb narrated: Ibn Idris narrated: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Some people claim that a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar to it, namely Abdullah ibn Salam. Abdullah only converted to Islam in Medina, and Masruq informed me that Surah Ha Mim was only revealed in Mecca, and that it was the argument of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his people, and he said: Have you considered if it is from God meaning the Qur’an and you disbelieved in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar to it and believed Moses and Muhammad, may God bless them both, are upon the Criterion. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Some people claim that the witness to something like it is Abdullah ibn Salam, but Abdullah only converted to Islam in Medina. Masruq informed me that Al-Ha Meem was only revealed in Mecca, and it was the Messenger of God’s argument with his people, so he said: Say, ‘Have you considered if it is from God’ meaning the Criterion and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to something like it, so the Torah is like the Criterion. Moses testified to the Torah, and Muhammad testified to the Criterion, may God bless them both and grant them peace. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, regarding His statement, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God?’… the verse, he said: Ibn Salam’s conversion to Islam occurred in Medina, and this surah was revealed in Mecca. It was only a dispute between Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people, so He said, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to something similar to it?’ He said: The Torah is like the Criterion, and Moses is like Muhammad, so he believed in him, and you were arrogant. Then He said: This one from among Israel believed in his prophet and his book, and you were arrogant, so you denied your prophet and your book. Indeed, God does not guide.… until His statement, This is an ancient falsehood. Others said: What is meant by his statement, And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it, is Abdullah ibn Salam. They said: The meaning of the statement is, And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of this Qur’an, confirming it. They said: And the like of the Qur’an is the Torah. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Abdullah bin Yusuf al-Tanisi told us, he said: I heard Malik bin Anas narrating on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, on the authority of Amir bin Saad bin Abi Waqqas, on the authority of his father, he said: “I never heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say about anyone walking on the earth that he is from the people of Paradise except for Abdullah bin Salam. He said: And in him was revealed: ‘And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it.’” Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us: Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us: Shu’ayb bin Safwan told us: Abdul Malik bin Umair told us that Muhammad bin Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam said: Abdullah said: It was revealed regarding Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God’… until His saying then you believed and were arrogant. Ali bin Saeed bin Masruq Al-Kindi told me: Abu Muhammad bin Ya’la told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of my nephew Abdullah bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam: It was revealed regarding “And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it, so he believed, and you were arrogant. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God’… the verse, he said: “There was a man from the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, ‘Would you accept that `Abdullah ibn Salam judge between me and you? Do you believe?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ So he sent for `Abdullah ibn Salam and said, ‘Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God, written in the Torah and the Gospel?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ So the Jews refused, and `Abdullah ibn Salam became a Muslim.” Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hussein told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it, he said: Abdullah bin Salam. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “Say: Have you considered if it is from God...” The verse. We were told that Abdullah bin Salam believed in the Book of God, in His Messenger, and in Islam, and he was one of the Jewish rabbis. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar. He said: He is Abdullah ibn Salam. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to something similar, the witness was Abdullah ibn Salam, who was one of the rabbis and scholars of the Children of Israel. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the Jews, and they came to him. He asked them, saying: ‘Do you know that I am the Messenger of God and you find me written down with you in the Torah?’ They said: ‘We do not know what you say, and we disbelieve in what you have brought.’ He said: ‘Which man is Abdullah ibn Salam among you?’ They said: ‘Our scholar and the best of us.’ He said: ‘Would you be satisfied with him between me and you?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Abdullah ibn Salam, and he came to him and said: ‘What is your testimony, O Ibn Salam?’ He said: ‘I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God and that your book came from God.’ So he believed and they disbelieved. God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘So he believed and you were arrogant.’” Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, saying: Aouf narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, saying: It reached me that when `Abdullah ibn Salam wanted to convert to Islam, he said: Aouf narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, saying: It reached me that when `Abdullah ibn Salam wanted to convert to Islam, he said: O Messenger of God, the Jews know that I am one of their scholars, and that my father was one of their scholars, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God and that they find you written with them in the Torah, so send to so-and-so and so-and-so, and whoever he named from the Jews, and hide me in your house and ask them about me and about my father, for they will tell you that I am the most knowledgeable of them, and that my father is one of the most knowledgeable of them, and I will go out to them and bear witness that you are the Messenger of God and that they find you written with them in the Torah and that you were sent with guidance and the religion of truth. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did so, and he hid him in his house and sent to the Jews, and they entered upon him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is `Abdullah ibn Salam among you? They said: The most knowledgeable of us is himself and the most knowledgeable of us is his father. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Have you considered that if he becomes Muslim, will you be safe? They said: He will not become Muslim, three times. So he called him and he went out, then he said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, and that they find you written down with them in the Torah, and that you were sent with guidance and the religion of truth. The Jews said: We were not afraid of you for this, O Abdullah ibn Salam. So they went out as disbelievers, and God the Almighty revealed about that: “Say: Have you considered: if it is from God, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it and believes, while you are arrogant?” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it, so he believed, and you were arrogant, he said: This is Ibn Salam with God, he bore witness that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his book are true, and it is true in the Torah, so he believed, and you were arrogant. Abu Sharhabil al-Himsi told me: Abu al-Mughirah told us: Sufyan ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I went with him until we entered the Jewish church in Medina on their feast day. They disliked our entering upon them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: ‘O group of Jews, show me twelve men who testify that there is no god but Him and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. God will nullify the wrath He was angry with from every Jew under the sky!’ So they remained silent, but none of them answered him. Then a third time, but none of them answered. So he left, and I was with him. When we were about to leave, a man called from behind us: ‘Stay where you are, O Muhammad!’ He said: ‘So he came forward, and that man said: ‘Which man do you know among you, O group of Jews?’ They said: ‘By God, we do not know of any man among us who is more knowledgeable of the Book of God or more understanding of it than you, nor than your father, nor than your grandfather before your father.’ He said: ‘Then I bear witness by God that he is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom you find in the Torah and the Gospel.’ They said: He lied, then they responded to him and said evil things to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: ((You have lied, we will not accept your words. Just now you were praising him for the good things you did, but now that he has believed you have lied and said what you said, so we will not accept your words!)) He said: So we went out, and we were three: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, myself, and Abdullah bin Salam, so God revealed about him: “Say, ‘Have you considered, if it is from God?’”... the verse. And the correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that what Masruq said in interpreting that is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation, because His statement, “Say, ‘Have you considered: if it is from God and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it,’” is in the context of God Almighty’s rebuke of the polytheists of Quraysh, and His argument against them for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This verse is similar to all the verses before it, and neither the People of the Book nor the Jews were mentioned before that, so this verse is directed to it being revealed about them, and there is no indication that the speech was diverted from the stories of those about whom the report came in meaning. However, reports have been transmitted from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that it was meant by Abdullah ibn Salam, and most of the people of interpretation agree with this, and they were more knowledgeable about the meanings of the Qur’an, the reason for its revelation and what was intended by it, so the interpretation of the statement, since that was the case: And Abdullah ibn Salam, who is the witness from among the Children of Israel, testified to the like of it, meaning the like of the Qur’an, which is the Torah. That is his testimony that Muhammad is written in the Torah as a prophet, and you will find the Jews written with them in the Torah as he is written in the Qur’an. He is a prophet. And His statement, So he believed, and you were arrogant, means: So Abdullah bin Salam believed and confirmed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, and you, the group of Jews, were arrogant about believing in what Abdullah bin Salam believed in. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people, means: God does not grant success in finding the truth and guiding you to the straight path, and the disbelieving people who wronged themselves by incurring God’s wrath through their disbelief in Him.
46:11: God the Most High says: “And those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from among the Jews of the Children of Israel said to those who believed in him, ‘If your belief in Muhammad and what he brought you had been any good, you would not have preceded us in believing in him.’” This interpretation is according to the view of those who interpreted His statement, And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it, as meaning that it refers to Abdullah ibn Salam. However, according to the interpretation of those who interpreted it as referring to the polytheists of Quraysh, then the interpretation of His statement, And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘If it had been any good, they would not have preceded us to it,’ should be directed to referring to the polytheists of Quraysh. This is how Qatada interpreted it, and in his interpretation of it, he also left out his interpretation of His statement, And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it, as meaning that it refers to Abdullah ibn Salam. He mentioned the narration about him: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ He said: Those were some of the polytheists who said that: We are more honorable, we, we. If it had been good, so-and-so and so-and-so would not have preceded us to it. Indeed, God chooses for His mercy whomever He wills. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it.’ He said: This was said by some people who were more powerful than them in the Age of Ignorance. They said, By God, if this had been good, the sons of so-and-so would not have preceded us to it. God chooses for His mercy whomever He wills and honors whomever He wills. Blessed and Exalted be He. And His statement, And when they were not guided by it, God Almighty says: And when they did not see Muhammad and what he brought from God of guidance, so that they would be guided by it to the straight path, they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood,’ meaning: They will say, “This Qur’an that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought is from the ancient report of the ancients,” as God Almighty said, informing about them: And they say, ‘Legends of the ancients which he wrote down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening.’ (al-Furqan 25:5)
46:12: The Most High says: And before this Book, there was the Book of Moses, which is the Torah, a guide for the Children of Israel to follow and a mercy for them which We sent down to them. The speech was presented as a report about the Book without mentioning the full report, as the speech is sufficient to indicate its completion, and its completion is: And before it was a Book of Moses, which is the Torah, a guide and a mercy which We sent down in the Arabic language. The Arabs differed in their interpretation of this and in the nominative meaning of an Arabic tongue. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: the tongue and the Arab are in the accusative case. Some of them said that on the authority of made the book like the truth of the tongue. According to the one who made the tongue in the accusative case as a state, and made the book one of its attributes, the interpretation of the statement should be: And this book is in the Arabic tongue confirming the Torah, the book of Moses, that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that what he brought from God is the truth. As for the second statement that we have narrated from some of them, that he made the nominative case of the tongue confirming, this statement has no meaning because that would then be interpreted thus, except that the one who confirms himself, because the Arabic tongue is this book, unless he makes the Arabic tongue Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and directs his interpretation to: And this book, which is the Qur’an, confirms Muhammad, which is the Arabic tongue. Then that would be one face of interpretation. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His saying an Arabic tongue is an adjective for the book, and it is in the accusative case because it is in it: And this is a book that confirms the Torah and the Gospel in the Arabic tongue, so an Arabic tongue is derived from yesdiq because it is a verb, just as you say: I passed by a man standing, doing good, and I passed by a man standing doing good. He said: If the Arabic tongue had been raised, it would have been permissible as an adjective for the book. It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: And this is a Book confirming what was before it in an Arabic tongue. So according to this reading, the accusative case in his saying in an Arabic tongue is directed from two aspects: One of them is based on what I have explained, that the tongue is outside of his saying confirming, and the other: that it is a cut from the ha’ in between you. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that it is in the accusative case as a state of what is in confirming of the mention of the book, because his saying confirming is a verb, so the interpretation of the statement, if that is the case, is: This Qur’an confirms the book of Moses that Muhammad is a prophet sent in the Arabic language. And His saying, To warn those who have wronged, means: To warn this book that We sent down to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, those who have wronged themselves by disbelieving in God and worshipping other than Him. His statement, And good tidings to the doers of good, means: It is good tidings for those who obeyed God and did good in their faith and obedience to Him in this world, so good is the reward from God in the hereafter for their obedience to Him. In His statement, And good tidings, there are two ways of parsing: The nominative case is in apposition to the Book, meaning: And this is a confirming Book and good tidings to the doers of good. The accusative case is in apposition to the Book, meaning: And this is a confirming Book and good tidings to the doers of good. So if He replaces gives good tidings with good tidings or glad tidings, it is in the accusative case, just as you would say, I came to you to visit you and to honor you and to fulfill your right, meaning to visit you and honor you and fulfill your right. So honor and fulfillment are in the accusative case with an implied meaning. The reciters differed in their reading of linadhir. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz read it with a ta', meaning: Let you warn, O Muhammad. The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it with a ya', meaning: Let the Book warn. Whichever of the two readings that reciter reads, he is correct.
46:13: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ other than whom there is no god, and then remain steadfast in their belief in that, not mixing it with polytheism and not disobeying God in His commands and prohibitions, there will be no fear concerning them from the terrors and horrors of the Day of Resurrection, nor will they grieve over what they left behind after their death.
46:14: And His statement, Those are the companions of Paradise, God Almighty says: Those who said this statement and were righteous are the people of Paradise and its inhabitants. They will abide therein, meaning: they will remain there forever. As a reward for what they used to do, meaning: as a reward from Us to them, which We gave them for the righteous deeds they used to do in this world.
46:15: God Almighty says: And We have enjoined upon the son of Adam, concerning his parents, good treatment of them during their lifetime, and righteousness towards them during their lifetime and after their death. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement hasan. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as hasan with a damma on the ha', according to the interpretation I have described. The most knowledgeable reciters of Kufa read it as ihsanan with an alif, meaning: And we enjoined upon him to be good to them. Whichever of them he recites is correct, due to the similarity of the meanings and the prevalence of each reading among the reciters. And His statement, His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, means that God Almighty says: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment and dutifulness to them, because he was from them to him as a pregnancy, a birth, and a growth. Then God, the Most High, described the blessing of his mother, and what she experienced from him during the state of carrying him and giving birth to him, and alerted him to the duty he owes to her of dutifulness, and her deserving of his honor and good companionship. So He said, His mother carried him, meaning in her womb with hardship, meaning with difficulty, and gave birth to him with hardship, meaning: and gave birth to him with hardship, meaning with difficulty. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His mother carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty. He said: She carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan, regarding his statement, His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, they said: She carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, that Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, His mother carried him unwillingly, he said: It was difficult for her. The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase unwillingly. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it unwillingly with a fat-ha on the kaf, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it unwillingly with a damma on it. I have explained the difference of opinion among those who differed in this regard before, If it is fat-ha or if it is damma in Surat Al-Baqarah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings, with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement, And his carrying and weaning is thirty months, God Almighty says: And his mother carried him as a fetus in her womb and weaned him from breastfeeding, and weaned him from drinking milk is thirty months. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement and his weaning. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Al-Hasan Al-Basri, recited it as and his pregnancy and his weaning, meaning: his mother separated him with weaning and separation. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to recite it as and his pregnancy and his weaning, with the opening of the fa without an alif, meaning: and his mother separated him. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is what the reciters of the countries have said, because the authoritative reciters have agreed on it and what contradicts it is an exception. And his saying, until he reaches his prime, the people of interpretation differed regarding the age limit for that, and some of them said: thirty-three years. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: His prime is thirty-three years, and his maturity is forty years, and the excuse for which God excuses the children of Adam is sixty. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Until he reaches his prime. He said: Thirty-three. Others said it is reaching the age of maturity. Who said that? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ibn Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: The most severe is the patience when good deeds are recorded for him and bad deeds are recorded against him. We have previously explained that the word ashd is the plural of shadd and that it is the utmost of its strength and its fullness. If that is the case, then the thirty-three is more similar to it than a dream, because a person does not reach the fullness of his strength and the end of his strength in his dream. When the Arabs mention such a thing in speech, they connect one to the other, making both times close to each other, as God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night or half of it. You would hardly say, I know that you stand [in prayer] nearly an hour of the night or all of it, nor would you say, I took a little of my wealth or all of it. Rather, you would say, I took all of my wealth or all of it. So it is the same in His statement, until he reaches his full strength and reaches forty years. There is no doubt that the arrangement of the forty to the thirty-three is better and more similar, since what was intended by that was to bring one of them closer to the other than the arrangement of the fifteenth or the eighteenth. His saying, and he reached forty years of age, that was when God’s proof against him was complete, and the ignorance of his youth was removed from him, and he knew what was due to God in terms of the right to be dutiful to his parents. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, and he reached forty years of age, and his bad deeds had passed. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: “And he reached forty years of age. He said: ‘My Lord, appoint me among the Muslims.’” Until he reached the age of forty. And his evil deeds had already passed. And His statement, He said, ‘My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents,’ meaning, the Most High says: This human being, whom God had guided to the right path and who had recognized God’s right over him in what He required of him in terms of being dutiful to his parents, said, My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor, meaning, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me in making me aware of Your Oneness and guiding me to acknowledge that and act in obedience to You. And upon my parents, before me, and other than that of Your favor upon us, and inspired me with that. Its root is from the word waza’at which means you pushed a man towards something, meaning you pushed him towards it. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And inspire me to be grateful for Your favor, he said: Make me grateful for Your favor. And what Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, My Lord, inspire me, even if the meaning of the word is interpreted to mean it, it does not mean inspiring, according to the correct interpretation. And His statement, And that I do righteous deeds that please You, means that God Almighty says: Encourage me to do righteous deeds that please You, and that is to do deeds that are in obedience to Him and to obey His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement, And make my offspring righteous for me, means: And make my affairs righteous for me in my offspring whom You have given, by making them guides to faith in You, following what pleases You, and working in obedience to You. So He, the Most High, described him as being dutiful to fathers, mothers, sons, and daughters. And He mentioned that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. And His statement, Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am among the Muslims, God Almighty says, informing about what this man said: Indeed, I have repented to You, meaning: I have repented to You from my sins that I committed in my past days, and indeed, I am among the Muslims, meaning: I am among those who submit to You in obedience, who surrender to Your command and prohibition, and who obey Your judgment.
46:16: God Almighty says: Those who have this characteristic are the ones from whom the best of what they did in this world of righteous deeds will be accepted, and He will reward them for it and recompense them for it. And We overlook their misdeeds meaning: And He will pardon them for the misdeeds that they did in this world, and He will not punish them for them. For the companions of Paradise meaning: We will do that to them, as we did for the companions of Paradise and its people who are its people. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Al-Ghatrif, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Trustworthy Spirit, who said: “The good deeds and bad deeds of the servant will be brought and will be recompensed for one another. If one good deed remains, God will expand Paradise for him.” He said: “So I entered upon him and he increased it, and he narrated something similar to this hadith. I said: ‘What if the good deed is lost?’ He said: ‘Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. ’... the verse.” Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr called Umar, may God be pleased with them both, and said to him: I have given you a recommendation that you should memorize: God has a right at night that He does not accept during the day, a right that He does not accept during the night. No one has a voluntary prayer until he performs the obligatory prayer. The scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection will be heavy because they followed the truth in this world, and that was heavy for them. It is right for a scale in which nothing but the truth is placed to be heavy, and the scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection will be light because they followed falsehood in this world and that was light for them. It is right for a scale in which nothing but falsehood is placed to be light. Have you not seen that God mentioned the people of Paradise with their best deeds, and someone says: How do my deeds compare to the deeds of these people? That is because God Almighty overlooks their worst deeds and does not reveal them. Have you not seen that God mentioned the people of Hell with their worst deeds, so someone says: I am better in deeds than these people. That is because God returned to them their best deeds. Have you not seen that God has in His hand the power to destroy, and He wishes from God a wish that is not true. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as yattaqubal and wa-tajidhu with a damma on the ya’ between them, and on what the agent is not named, and they raised ahsan. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as nataqubal and wa-natajidhu with a noon and a fatha on it, and they lowered ahsan with the meaning of God Almighty informing them about Himself that He will do that to them, and in response to the statement of His statement, And We have enjoined upon man and We accept from them the best of what they did and overlook. They are two well-known readings with correct meaning, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. And His statement, The promise of truth which they were promised, means: God promised them this promise, the promise of truth, there is no doubt that He will fulfill it for them, which they were promised in this world after them, God Almighty. And His statement, The promise of truth, is in the accusative case because the source is outside of His statement, He accepts from them the best of what they did and overlooks their bad deeds. And He only excluded from this statement the source of He promised a promise, because His statement, He accepts from them and overlooks is a promise from God to them, so He said, The promise of truth, according to that meaning.
46:17: And this is a description from God, the Most High, with which we describe a misguided disbeliever, and a disobedient one towards his parents, while they are striving to advise him and call him to God. Their calling him to the truth and their advice to him only increases his insolence and rebellion against God, and his persistence in his ignorance. God, the Most High, says: And he who said to his parents, that they called him to belief in God, and the acknowledgment of God’s resurrection of His creation from their graves, and His recompense to them for their deeds, Fie upon you both, meaning: filth and stench upon you. Do you promise me that I will come forth? meaning: Do you promise me that I will come forth from my grave after my annihilation and trial, alive? As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Do you promise me that I will come out? That I will be resurrected after death. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Do you promise me that I will come forth? He said: He means the resurrection after death. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you! Do you promise me that I will come forth?’… to the end of the verse. He said: The one who said this was a son of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. He said, Do you promise me that I will come forth?: Do you promise me that I will be resurrected after death? Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth?’ He said: He is the disbelieving, immoral person who is disobedient to his children and denies the resurrection. Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: Then he described a bad servant who was disobedient to his parents and wicked, saying: And he who said to his parents, ‘Fie upon you both’... until His saying: Legends of the ancients. And His statement: And generations have passed before me means: Do you promise me that I will be resurrected, while generations have passed before me, and they perished and none of them were resurrected? And if I were to be resurrected after my death, as you say, then those generations who perished before me would have been resurrected. And they are calling upon God means, the Most High said, and his parents are calling upon God to help him, and they are calling upon Him to believe in God and acknowledge the resurrection, and they are saying to him, Woe to you! Believe, meaning, believe in God’s promise and acknowledge that you will be resurrected after your death. Indeed, the promise of God, which He promised His creation, that He will raise them from their graves and bring them forth from them to the place of reckoning to be rewarded for their deeds, is true, without doubt. So the enemy of God says, responding to his parents and rejecting their advice, and denying God’s promise: What is this that you are saying to me and calling me to, that I will be resurrected after my death from my grave, except what the people of old wrote of falsehoods, so they wrote it, and you two were right and spoke the truth.
46:18: God Almighty says: These are the ones who have this description, upon whom God’s punishment is due, and upon whom His chastisement and wrath have befallen, among those upon whom God’s punishment has befallen in the same way as it befell these nations of the jinn and mankind who have passed away, who denied God’s messengers and rebelled against the command of their Lord. And His statement, Indeed, they were losers, means that God Almighty says: They were the ones who were deceived by selling guidance for misguidance and comfort for punishment. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The jinn do not die. Qatada said: So I said: Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect among nations that have passed on.
46:19: And His statement, And for all are degrees according to what they have done, the Most High says: For all of these two groups: the group of belief in God and the Last Day and being dutiful to parents, and the group of disbelief in God and the Last Day and being disobedient to parents, whose characteristics our Lord, the Most High, has described in these verses, are stations and ranks with God on the Day of Resurrection, according to what they have done, meaning from the deeds that they do in this world, whether good or bad, God will reward them for them. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And for all are degrees according to what they have done, that the degrees of the people of Hell will go downward, and the degrees of the people of Paradise will go upward. And that He may fully recompense them for their deeds, that is, the Most High says, “And that He may give all of them the rewards for the deeds that they did in this world. The good-doer among them will receive, through his goodness, what God has promised of honor, and the evil-doer among them will receive only punishment for his sin, not for what he did not do, nor will he be held responsible for the sin of another. The good-doer among them will not be deprived of the reward for his goodness.
46:20: God Almighty says, And on the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them, ‘You consumed your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them.’ Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire, Yazid recited until he reached, and for what you used to commit, you know, by God, that some people keep their good deeds. A man kept his good deeds back if he was able, and there is no power except with God. It was mentioned that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say, If I wished, I would have the best food among you and the softest clothing among you, but I keep my good deeds back. It was mentioned to us that when he came to Syria, food was prepared for him, the likes of which had never been seen before. He said, This is for us, but what about the poor Muslims who died without being satisfied with barley bread? Khalid ibn al-Walid said, Paradise is for them. Umar’s eyes welled up, and he said, If our share is in the ruins, and they have gone - Abu Ja`far said, As far as I can see - with Paradise, then they have been far removed from us.” “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon the people of the Suffa, a place where the poor Muslims gathered, and they were patching their clothes with leather as they could not find any patches for them. He said: ‘Are you better today, or is it a day when one of you goes out in the morning in one garment and returns in another, and is fed with a bowl and taken away with another, and his house is covered as the Kaaba is covered?’ They said: ‘We will be better on that day.’ He said: ‘Rather, you are better today.’” Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, who said: Saheb told us on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “Our food with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only two black things: water and dates. By God, we did not see this brown one of yours, nor did we know what it was.” He said: Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Abu Burda bin Abdullah bin Qais Al-Ash’ari on the authority of his father: “O my son, if you had witnessed us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were with our Prophet when the rain fell upon us, you would have thought that our scent was the scent of sheep, for our clothing was wool.” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God Almighty: You have spent your good things in your worldly life… to the end of the verse. Then he recited: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived. And he recited: “Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We give him thereof.” And he recited: Whoever desires the immediate - We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend.… to the end of the verse. And he said: These are the ones who spent their good things in their worldly life. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement, You have gone away, your good things. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as you have gone away without a question, except for Abu Ja`far al-Qari`, who recited it as a question. The Arabs ask questions with rebuke and leave out the question in it, so they say, Did you go away and do such and such? or Did you go away, so you did, and Did you do? The more impressive of the two recitations is the omission of the question in it, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and because it is the more eloquent of the two languages. And His statement, So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation, God Almighty says: It will be said to them: So today, O disbelievers who consumed your good things in their worldly life, you will be recompensed, meaning you will be rewarded with the punishment of humiliation, meaning the punishment of disgrace, and that is the punishment of the Fire that humiliates them. Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: The punishment of humiliation means humiliation. Because you were arrogant upon the earth without right means: because you were arrogant in this world on the face of the earth towards your Lord, refusing to devote worship to Him alone and to submit to His commands and prohibitions without right, that is, without what your Lord has permitted and authorized you to do. And because you were wicked means: because you disobeyed Him therein and rebelled against Him.
46:21: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And mention, O Muhammad, to your people who reject you, what you have brought them of the truth, Hud, the brother of Aad. Indeed, God has sent you to them as He had sent him to Aad. So, fear that the punishment of God will befall them for their disbelief, as befell them when they denied Our Messenger Hud to them, when he warned his people, Aad, of Al-Ahqaf. Al-Ahqaf is the plural of Haqf, which is a sand dune that is long and not yet a mountain. Al-A'sha meant it: So he spent the night in Artah, surrounded by a hole in the north, leaving his face dark. The commentators differed about the location of this Ahqaf. Some of them said: It is a mountain in the Levant. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, my father said, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf. He said: A mountain in Syria. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf, that it is a mountain called Al-Ahqaf. Others said: Rather, it is a valley between Oman and Mahra. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: He told me, he told me, he told me, my uncle told me, he told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf. He said: Al-Ahqaf, which Hud warned his people, is a valley between Oman and Mahrah. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: The dwellings of the people of Ad and their community, when God sent Hud to them, were in al-Ahqaf 46:the sand between Oman and Hadhramaut and all of Yemen. And despite that, they had spread throughout the land, conquering its people by virtue of the strength that God had given them. Others said: It is land. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Al-Ahqaf is the land. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf. He said: Hashaf or a word similar to it. Abu Musa said: They say mustahashaf. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf Hashaf from Hasma. Others said: It is sand overlooking the sea with trees. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf, he told us that Aad were a tribe in Yemen, people of sand overlooking the sea in a land called Ash-Shihr. Muhammad Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf, he said: It has reached us that they were on a land called Ash-Shihr, overlooking the sea, and they were people of sand. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Amr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The dwellings of Ad were in Ash-Shihr. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty informed that the brother of Hud warned the people of Aad about Al-Ahqaf, and Al-Ahqaf is what was described of the elevated rectangular sands, as Al-Ajjaj said: He went to Artah, Haqf Ahqfa And as Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said in his statement, And remember the brother of Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf, he said: Al-Ahqaf is the sand that is in the form of a mountain, which the Arabs call Al-Haqf, and Al-Ahqaf is only from sand. He said: And the brother of Aad was Hud. And it is possible that it was a mountain in the Levant, and it is possible that it was a valley between Oman and Hadhramaut, and it is possible that it was Ash-Shihr, and in knowing it there is no fulfillment of an obligation, and in ignorance of it there is no neglect of an obligation, and wherever he was, his description is as we have described, that they were a people whose dwellings were the high, rectangular sands. And His statement, And there have been warnings before him and after him that you shall not worship except God, God Almighty says: And the messengers have passed away with warning their nations, before him, meaning: before Hud and after him, meaning: and after Hud. It has been mentioned that this is in the recitation of Abdullah, And there have been warnings before him and after him, “that you shall not worship except God, meaning: Do not associate anything with God in your worship of Him, but devote worship to Him alone, and single out divinity for Him, for there is no god other than Him. And they were, as has been mentioned, people of idols that they worshipped instead of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? It was narrated that Al-Husayn said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And there have been warnings before him and after him that you shall not worship except God, that God will not send a messenger except that God be worshipped. And His saying, Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day, God Almighty says, informing about what Hud said to his al-Nas 114:Indeed, I fear for you, O people, because of your worship of other than God, the punishment of God on a tremendous Day. And that is a Day whose terror is great, and that is the Day of Resurrection.
46:22: God Almighty says: The people of Aad said to Hud, when he said to them, "Worship none but God. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible Day." Hud said, Have you come to us to turn us away from the worship of our gods to the worship of what you call us to, and to follow you in your words? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? He said: To send us down. And he recited, He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been patient with them. He said: To lead us astray, to remove us, and to turn us away. Then bring us what you promise us of punishment for our worship of the gods we worship, if you are among the people of truth in his words and his promises.
46:23: God Almighty says: Hood said to his people, Aad: The knowledge of the time of the coming of what He promised you of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him is only with God. I do not know of that except what He taught me. And I will convey to you that with which I have been sent. He says: I am only a messenger to you from God, conveying and conveying to you what He sent me with of the message. But I see that you are a people who are ignorant of the places of your own interests, so you do not know what harm there is to them by your worship of other than God, and in hastening His punishment.
46:24: God Almighty says: So when the punishment of God, which they had hastened, came to them, they saw it as a cloud rising in a part of the sky, facing their valleys. The Arabs call the clouds that are seen in some parts of the sky in the evening, and then the next day they become even and some of them creep towards others, a cloud, because of their appearance in some parts of the sky when they arise, as Al-A’sha said: O you who see a spectacle that I have been staring at, as if lightning were flames on its edges. They said, This is a cloud that will bring us rain. They thought that seeing it meant that rain had come to revive them. They said, This is what Hud promised us, and it is rain. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys… the verse. And it was mentioned to us that the rain was withheld from them for a period of time, and when they saw the punishment approaching, they said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ And it was mentioned to us that they said, Hud has lied. So when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and smelled it, he said, Rather, it is that which you were hastening, a wind within which is a painful punishment. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: God drove the black cloud that Qayl ibn Anzah had chosen, with all the punishment it contained, to the tribe of Aad, until it came out upon them from a valley of theirs called Al-Mughith. When they saw it, they were filled with good tidings, They said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ God Almighty says: Rather, it is what you were impatient for - a wind within which is a painful punishment. And His statement, Rather, it is that which you hastened, says the Most High, informing us of what His Prophet Hud said to his people when they said to him upon seeing a cloud of punishment appearing to them in the sky: This is a cloud of rain by which we may live. It is not a cloud of rain, but rather a cloud of punishment for you. Rather, it is that which you hastened, meaning, it is the punishment which you hastened, so you said: Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful. “A wind in which is a painful punishment.” The wind is repeated in His statement, It is that which you hastened, as if it was said, Rather, it is a wind in which is a painful punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of `Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Hud was a brave man among his people. He was sitting among his people when a cloud came, and they said, This is a cloud bringing us rain. He said, Rather, it is that which you were hastening, a wind in which is a painful punishment. He said, A wind came and began to throw down the tent, and to bring the absent man and throw him down. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, he said: The wind would blow it away and lift it until it looked like a locust. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, to the end of the verse, he said: It is the wind when it stirs up clouds, They said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ So their prophet said: Rather, it is a wind in which is a painful punishment.
46:25: And His saying, It destroys everything by the command of its Lord: God Almighty says: It destroys everything and throws some of it upon others, destroying it, as Jarir said: And you will have been like the people of Thamud when they roared their backs and destroyed them completely. What he means by his saying: He destroyed them: He threw some of them on top of others, dead and dying. What he meant by his saying, It destroys everything by the command of its Lord, is what it was sent to destroy, because it did not destroy Hud and those who believed in him.
