Abu Kuraib told us: Talq told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God did not send upon the Aad people a wind except the size of this ring of mine, so he took off his ring. His saying, So they woke up and nothing could be seen except their dwellings, means: So the people of Hud woke up and were destroyed and nothing could be seen in their country except the dwellings in which they used to live. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, So at night nothing is seen except their dwellings. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as: You will not see except their dwellings with the ta in the accusative case, meaning: So at night you, O Muhammad, will not see except their dwellings. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as: You will not see except their dwellings with the ya in yarea and the dwellings in the nominative case, meaning: what was described before that nothing is seen in their country except their dwellings. Al-Hasan Al-Basri narrated: You will not see with the ta in the accusative case. And whichever of the two readings mentioned from the people of Medina and Kufa did that reader read, he is correct, which is the reading with the raising of the dwellings if his saying yaru is read with the ya’ and its damma, and with the accusative of the dwellings if his saying yaru is read with the ta’ and its fatha. As for that which was related from al-Hasan, it is ugly in Arabic even if it is permissible. It is only ugly because the Arabs mention the verbs that come before illa, even if the nouns that come after it are female nouns. So you say: Ma qama illa akhtika no one stood up except your sister, Ma ja’ani illa jarikat no one came to me except your slave girl, and they hardly ever say: Ma ja’ani illa jarikat no one came to me except your slave girl, and that is because the deletion before illa no one, or one thing, and something mentions the Arabs, even if they mean the feminine, so you say: If one of them comes to you, honor him, and they do not say: If she comes to you. Al-Farra’ allowed it out of compulsion, and it is mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited to him: And your fire, you have never seen a fire like it. You know that Ma'ad is the most generous. So he made the verb feminine because it refers to fire. He said: The best way to say is: Nothing like it has been seen. And His statement, Thus do We recompense the criminal people, God Almighty says: Just as We recompensed the ‘Ad people for their disbelief in God with punishment in this world, and destroyed them with Our torment, thus do We recompense the disbelieving people among Our creation, when they persisted in their transgression and rebelled against their Lord.
46:26: God Almighty says to the infidels of Quraysh 106:And We have certainly empowered, O people of ‘Ad, whom We destroyed for their disbelief, in that which We did not empower you in of this world, and We gave them from it that which We did not give you from them of an abundance of wealth, spacious bodies, and strong physiques. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We have certainly empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you, meaning We have not empowered you. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We have empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you, He informed you that He gave the people what He did not give you. And His statement, And We gave them hearing with which they hear the admonitions of their Lord, and sight with which they see the proofs of God, and hearts with which they understand what is evil and what is good for them. Their hearing, their sight, and their hearts availed them nothing. He says: What He gave them of hearing, sight, and hearts did not benefit them at all, because they did not use them for what they were given, and they did not use them in what would save them from God’s punishment. Rather, they used them in what would keep them safe from His wrath. Because they denied the signs of God He says: Because they were lying about God’s proofs, even though they were His messengers, and they denied their prophethood. And that which they ridiculed overtook them He says: What they ridiculed returned to them, and what they were angry with befell them, so they hastened the punishment. This is a warning from God, may He be glorified, to the Quraysh, saying to them: Beware of the punishment that befell the ‘Ad for your disbelief in God and your denial of His messengers, and hasten to repent. Before the curse.
46:27: God Almighty says to the infidels of Quraysh, warning them of His might and power that He would bring upon them because of their disbelief: And We have destroyed, O people, of the towns around your town, such as the Rock of Thamud, the land of Sodom, Ma’rib, and the like. So We warned their people with examples and destroyed their homes, making them desolate on their roofs. And His saying, And We explained the signs, means: We admonished them with various kinds of admonitions, and reminded them with various kinds of remembrance and arguments, and made that clear to them. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And We have explained the signs, he said, that they may return, meaning that they may return from what they were upon, which was disbelief in God and His signs. And in the speech there is something that was omitted, the mention of which was neglected because the speech indicated it, and it is: “But they refused except to remain in their disbelief and persist in their error, so We destroyed them. No helper from Us will aid them.” God, the Most High, says: “Why did not those whom We destroyed from the nations before them, their idols and their gods, which they took as a sacrifice to their Lord, by which they claimed to draw near to their Lord, aid Us when Our punishment came to them, and save them from Our punishment, if they interceded for them with their Lord as they claim?” This is an argument from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, against the polytheists of his people, saying to them: “If your gods that you worship besides God were of any use to you, or of any benefit to God, as you claim that you only worship them to bring you nearer to God, then I would have been sufficient for those who came before you from the nations that I destroyed because of their worship of them, so I would have warded off the punishment from them when it descended, or they would have interceded for them with their Lord. They were in their worship like you, but it harmed them and did not benefit them.” God the Almighty says: Rather, they have gone astray from them. He says: Rather, their gods that they used to worship have abandoned them and taken a path other than theirs, because their worshippers were destroyed, and they were stones or copper, so what happened to them did not happen to them. They called upon them, but they did not answer them or help them. That is their going astray from them, and that is their lie. God the Almighty says: These gods that have gone astray from those who used to invent, so they say: They bring us closer to God, they are our intercessors with God. He presented the statement in the form of a verb, and the meaning is the one done to, so it was said: That is their lie, and the meaning in it is: the one who was lied to because the lie is the one who lies, and the gods are the ones who are lied to. Similar examples of that have been explained before. He said: Likewise, His statement: And they did not invent. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement and that is their slander, so the majority of the reciters of the regions read it: and that is their slander with a kasra on the alif, a sukoon on the fa’, and a damma on the kaf, with the meaning that we explained. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, narrated in this regard: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Al-Qasim told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite it as and that is their most misguided, meaning with the alif and the kaf open. He said: the most misguided of them. So whoever recites the first recitation, which is followed by the reciters of the regions, then the ha and the meem are in the genitive case. And whoever recites this recitation which we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, then the ha and the meem are in the accusative case, because the meaning of the speech in this case is: And that is what turned them away from believing in God. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading that is followed by the readings of the regions, due to the consensus of the authorities on it.
46:28: His saying, “Why then did not those whom they took as deities besides God aid them? Rather, they have gone astray from them. That is their falsehood and what they have been inventing.”
46:29: God Almighty says, rebuking the infidels of Quraysh for their disbelief in what the jinn believed in: And when We directed to you, O Muhammad, a group of jinn listening to the Qur’an. He mentioned that they were directed to the Messenger of God, may God bless them and grant them peace, by the incident of stoning them with meteors. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: “The jinn were listening, but when they did not stone, they said: ‘What happened in the sky is due to something that happened on Earth.’ So they went searching until they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, coming out of the Ukaz market praying the dawn prayer with his companions, so they went to their people.” Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, the heavens were guarded. Satan said: ‘I was only guarded for something that has happened on earth.’ So he sent out his troops to the earth, and they found the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing praying the dawn prayer with his companions at Nakhlah, and he was reciting. They listened until he finished: ‘And they turned back to their people as warners’... until His saying: ‘straight’.” Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of my uncle, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an… to the end of the verse, he said: “The sky was not guarded during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and they would sit in places to listen. Then when God sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the sky was guarded with a strong guard, and the devils were stoned. They denied that and said: ‘We do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them a right course.’ Iblis said: ‘An event has occurred on earth,’ and the jinn gathered around him. He said: ‘Disperse on earth and inform me of this report that has occurred in heaven.’ The first dispatch was a group from the people of Nasibin, who were the nobles and leaders of the jinn. So he sent them to Tihamah, and they pushed on until they reached the valley, the valley of Nakhal, and they found the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, praying the dawn prayer in the valley of Nakhal, and they listened. When they heard him reciting the Qur’an, they said: ‘Listen.’” The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know that they had listened to him reciting the Qur’an. When he had finished, they turned back to their people as warners. The people of interpretation differed regarding the number of people about whom God said, And when We directed to you a group of the jinn, some of them said: They were seven people. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Abdul Hamid told us: Al-Nadr ibn Arabi told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an… the verse. He said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them messengers to their people. Others said: Rather, there were nine people. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, And when We turned to you a company of the jinn, he said: They were nine people, among them was a whirlwind. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaysh, he said: “The revelation was sent down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Batn Nakhal, and when they attended him, he said: There were nine of them, one of them was Zuba’ah.” His saying, When they attended him, means: When these people from the jinn whom God had sent to His Messenger, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, attended. Scholars differed about the manner in which they were present with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: They were present with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to learn about the matter that had occurred before him, what had occurred in the heavens, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in their place, as we mentioned from Ibn Abbas before. And as Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not notice them until they came, and God Almighty revealed to him about them, and informed him about them. Others said: Rather, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that the Qur’an be recited to them, and that they gathered for him after God had warned them and ordered him to recite the Qur’an to them. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an, he said: “It was mentioned to us that they were directed to him from Nineveh. He said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have been commanded to recite the Qur’an to the jinn, so which of you will follow me?’ So they lowered their heads. Then he asked them to follow him, and they lowered their heads. Then he asked a third to follow him, and they lowered their heads. A man said: ‘You are indeed a man of action,’ so ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud followed him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered a valley called the Valley of al-Hujun. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line over ‘Abdullah to make him stand firm. So I began to fall and I saw things like eagles walking in their tambourines, and I heard a great noise until I feared for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited the Qur’an. When the Prophet of God returned, I said: ‘O Prophet of God, what is the noise that you heard?’ He said: ‘They gathered around me regarding a slain person who had been among them, and justice was passed between them.’ And he mentioned to us…” When Ibn Masoud came to Kufa, he saw some old men from the Zutt tribe, and they were frightened by him. He said: Among these are some foreigners. He said: “I have never seen anyone from the jinn who resembled the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, more closely than these.” Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated: Ibn Thawr narrated from Muammar from Qatada, “That the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went and Ibn Mas'ud went one night and called the jinn. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line over Ibn Mas'ud and said to him: Do not leave it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the jinn and recited the Qur’an to them. Then he returned to Ibn Mas'ud and said: Did you see anything? He said: I heard a great deal of noise. He said: The jinn argued about a person who had been killed among them, and it was decided between them justly. They asked him for provisions, and he said: Every bone of yours is a vein, and every dung of yours is green. They said: O Messenger of God, God detests them to us. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade one of them from using one of them for istinja cleaning oneself after relieving oneself. When Ibn Mas'ud came to Kufa, he saw the Zutt, who were tall, black people, and they frightened him. He said: Come out. It was said to him: These are the Zutt people. How similar they are to the men who were sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Katheer, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Ghailan al-Thaqafi, that he said to Ibn Mas`ud: “I was told that you were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the delegation of the jinn.” He said: Yes. He said: How was it? Then he mentioned the entire hadith. He mentioned that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line over him and said: Do not leave it. Then he mentioned that something like black smoke covered the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was frightened three times, until it was close to dawn. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me and said: Did you sleep? I said: “No, by God, and I thought many times to seek help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your staff, saying: “Sit down.” He said: If I went out, I would not be safe from some of them snatching you away. Then he said: Did you see anything? He said: Yes, I saw black men with white hairs in their hair. He said: “Those were the jinn of Nasibin. They asked me for provisions—and provisions are provisions—so I gave them every broken bone, dung, or excrement. I said: “O Messenger of God, what good is that?” About them? He said: They will not find a bone but they will find its flesh on it on the day it was eaten, nor a dung but they will find its seeds in it on the day it was eaten. So let none of you clean himself when he comes out of the toilet with a bone, dung, or dung.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: Abu Zur’ah Wahb ibn Rashid told us: Yunus said: Shihab said: Abu Uthman ibn Shabah Al-Khuza’i, who was from the people of Ash-Sham, told me that Ibn Mas’ud said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions while he was in Mecca: ‘Whoever among you would like to attend the meeting of the jinn tonight, let him do so.’ No one from among them attended except me. So we set off until we were at the top of Mecca. He drew a line for me with his foot, then ordered me to sit in it. Then he set off until he stood up and began to recite the Qur’an. A great black cloud came between him and me and prevented me from hearing his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of clouds, going away, until only a group of them remained. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished at dawn and went to relieve himself. Then he came to me and said: ‘What happened to the group?’ I said: ‘They are them, O Messenger of God.’ He took a bone, dung, or a skull and gave it to them as provisions, then he forbade anyone from using perfume or dung.” Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told us: Sayunis told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Uthman ibn Shabah al-Khuza’i, who was from the people of Ash-Sham, that Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “He mentioned something similar, except that he said: So he gave them an inheritance or a bone as provisions, and he did not mention the skull.” Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman bin Wahb told me, he said: He told me, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, that Ibn Masoud said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I spent the night reciting to the jinn a quarter of Surat Al-Hujun. They differed about the place where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an to them. Abdullah bin Masoud said that he recited it to them at Al-Hujun, and we have forgotten the narration from us about that. Others said: He read to them in Nakhal. We mentioned some of those who said that, and we criticized those we did not mention. Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Khallad narrated to us on the authority of Zuhair bin Muawiyah on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The group of people who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the jinn of Nasibin came to him while he was in Nakhalah.” Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn. He said: He met them at a palm tree that night. And His saying, So when they were present at it, they said, ‘Listen,’ God Almighty says: So when they were present at the Qur’an, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting, some of them said to one another, Listen, so that we may listen to the Qur’an. As Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, So when they attended to him, they said, ‘Be quiet.’ They said, Shh. He said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Asim on the authority of Zur bin Habish, similarly. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, So when they attended him, they said, ‘Listen.’ The people knew that they would not understand until they listened. And his saying, When it was finished, means: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished reading and reciting the Qur’an. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So when it was concluded meaning: When he finished the prayer, they turned back to their people as warners. And His statement, they turned back to their people as warners means: They turned back as warners of God’s punishment for disbelief in Him. It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them messengers to their people. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: An-Nadr narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. This statement contradicts the statement that was narrated from him, that he said: The Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did not know that they listened to him while he was reciting the Quran, because it is impossible that he would send them to others except after he knew where they were, unless it is said: He did not know where they were while they were listening to the Quran, and then after they had returned to their people, so he sent them as messengers to their people at that time, and that is not the report that was narrated.
46:30: God Almighty says, informing about what was said by those jinn who were sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to their people when they returned to them from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O our people from the jinn we have heard a book revealed after the book of Moses confirming what was before it meaning: it confirms what came before it of the books of God that He sent down to His messengers. His saying, guides to the truth, means: it directs to what is right, and indicates what pleases God. And to a straight path, means: and to a path that is free of crookedness, which is Islam. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that he read: They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it and guiding to the truth and to a straight path.’ He said: How quickly the people understood! It was mentioned to us that they were diverted to him from Nineveh.
46:31: God Almighty says, informing us of what was said by these men of the jinn: O our people, from the jinn, respond to the caller of God, they said: Respond to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to what he calls you to of obedience to God. And believe in him, meaning: And believe him in what he and his people brought to you of God’s commands and prohibitions, and other things that he called you to believe in. He will forgive you, meaning: Your Lord will cover your sins for you and conceal them for you and will not disgrace you for them in the Hereafter by punishing you for them. And save you from a painful punishment, meaning: And He will save you from a painful punishment if you repent from your sins and turn from your disbelief to faith in God and His caller.
46:32: And His statement, And whoever does not respond to the Caller to God will not be able to frustrate Him on the earth, the Almighty says, informing about what these people said to their al-Nas 114:And whoever, O people, does not respond to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Muhammad, and His caller to what he was sent to call to of His Oneness and to work in obedience to Him, will not be able to frustrate Him on the earth, meaning he will not frustrate his Lord by fleeing if He wants to punish him for his denial of His caller and his failure to believe in him, even if he goes on the earth fleeing because wherever he is he is in His power and control. And he will have no protectors besides Him, meaning: And whoever responds to the Caller to God besides his Lord will have no helpers to aid him from God if his Lord punishes him for his disbelief and denial of His caller. His statement, Those are in manifest error, means: These are the ones who did not respond to God’s caller and believe in Him and in what He called them to of monotheism and working in obedience to Him, in injustice towards the straight path, and taking it in a way that is not right. Clear means: It is clear to whoever contemplates it that it is misguidance and taking it without intention.
46:33: God Almighty will say: Have these deniers not considered that God revives His creation after their death, and raises them from their graves after their affliction, saying to their fathers and mothers, Fie on you both! Do you promise me that I will come forth, while generations before me have passed away? (al-Ahqaf 46:17)? But they have not been sent with the sight of their hearts, so that they may see and know that God, who created the seven heavens and the earth, and originated them from nothing, and was not weary of creating them, so that He would be unable to invent or bring them into existence, is able to bring the dead to life, so that He brings them forth from their affliction in their graves alive as they were before their death. The Arabists differed about the reason for the introduction of the preposition ba in His saying bi-Qadir. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: This preposition is like the preposition ba in His saying God is sufficient, which is like tanbata bi-dahn the oil grows (Surat al-Mu’minun 23:20). Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: This preposition ba was introduced for al-k. He said: The Arabs introduce it with negation if it is raising what precedes it, and they introduce it if a verb that requires two nouns is placed upon it, like your saying: I do not think you are standing, and I was not standing, and I died, you were standing. So if you remove the preposition ba, it makes the object in which it acts, in the accusative case, with what it acts upon of the verb. He said: If you remove the preposition ba from Qadir in this position, it raises it because it is the predicate of lan. He said: And some of them recited to me: The camel of Hakim bin Al-Musayyab did not return disappointed. So, the preposition ba was inserted into a verb, and if you threw it, it would be nasb with the verb, not with the preposition ba. Similar things can be compared to this. He said to some of those who rejected the statement of Al-Basri that we mentioned, his statement: This ba was entered for denial because the denied is in the meaning, even if there was a separation between them by or they did not see that God is able to revive the dead, K said: So the name yaruwa and what follows it in its connection, the ba is not entered into it, but its meaning is denial, so it was entered for the meaning. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Basri that he refused to include except, and that the grammarians of Kufa permitted it, and said: I did not think that Zaid was anything but standing, and I did not think that Zaid was a learned man, so it was included for the sake of meaning. It was narrated that Al-Basri refused to include the word except, and that the grammarians of Kufa permitted it, saying: I never thought that Zayd was anything but standing, and I never compared Zayd to anything but a scholar. And he recited: I swear that I gave birth to none of them blindly, except Ziyad. He said: So it was inserted only after answering the oath. He said: As for God is sufficient, this was not inserted for a correct meaning, and it is for amazement, as you say for a circumstance of Zayd. He said: As for growth with oil, they agreed that it is a relative clause. The most similar of the sayings in that regard to the one who said: The preposition with was inserted in His statement able for denial, because of what we mentioned to the reasons for those who said that. The reciters differed in reading the statement of God, Baqadeer able. The majority of the countries read it this way. Abu Ishaq, Al-Jahdary and Al-A'raj read it as Baqadeer and this is the correct reading according to us due to the consensus of the reciters of the countries on it. As for the others whom I mentioned, according to what was reported from them, they read it as Yaqadeer with a ya. It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, it was said that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able without a ba, so in that is an argument for those who read it as Qadeer with a ya and an alif. And His statement, Yes, He is over all things competent means, the Most High says: Yes, He who created the heavens and the earth is able to bring the dead to life: meaning, the One who created that, over everything He willed to create and wanted to do, has power that nothing He willed is unable to do, and nothing He wanted to do could tire Him out. Creating creation after annihilation would tire Him out, because whoever is unable to do that is weak. So, someone who is weak in what He wanted should not be a god.
46:34: God the Most High says: And on the Day when these deniers of the Resurrection and God's reward for His servants for their good deeds and His punishment for their evil deeds will be exposed to the Fire, the Fire of Hell, it will be said to them then: Is not this the punishment that you are being punished with today - which you used to deny in this world - the truth? As a rebuke from God for their denial of it in this world. “They will say: Yes, by our Lord.” He says: These disbelievers will respond immediately with that, by saying: Yes, it is the truth, and God said: Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. He says: The one who confirmed that will say to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire now for what you used to deny in this world, and reject, and make a confession when you are called to believe in it.
46:35: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, confirming his determination to carry out the burden of the message and the heavy loads of prophethood, peace and blessings be upon him, and commanding him to follow the example of those who were resolute before him from among His messengers who were patient in the face of the great hardships they encountered from their people and the harm and hardships they suffered from them. So be patient, O Muhammad, in the cause of God, with the harm that befell you from your people, to whom We sent you with warning, just as those of resolute determination were patient in carrying out God’s command and adhering to His obedience from among His messengers, whom He did not forbid from carrying out His command despite the hardships they suffered from it. It was said: Those of them who were determined were those who were tested in the cause of God in this world with trials, and the trials only increased their perseverance in the cause of God, like Noah, Abraham, Moses, and those like them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Thawaba bin Masoud told me, on the authority of Ata’ al-Haraasani, that he said: So be patient as were patient the messengers of strong will - Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, may God bless them and grant them peace. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will. We were told that Abraham was one of them. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement, So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will, that all the messengers were of strong will. God did not take a messenger except one of strong will, so be patient as they were patient. Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will, he said: God called him strong will because of his strong will. And His statement, And do not hasten them means: Do not hasten them with the punishment. He says: Do not hasten your asking your Lord for that, for that will inevitably befall them. It will be as if, on the Day they see what they are promised, they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour of a day. He says: It will be as if, on the Day they see the punishment of God that He promises them, that it will befall them, they had not remained in this world for an hour of a day, because He makes them forget the severity of what will befall them of His punishment, the amount of time they stayed in this world, and the amount of years and months they stayed in it, as He, the Most High, said: He will say, ‘How many years did you stay on the earth?’ They will say, ‘We stayed a day or part of a day, so ask the counters.’ (al-Mu’minun 23:112-113) His saying, a notification has two interpretations: One of them is that its meaning is: They did not remain except for an hour of the day, that was a notification, meaning: that was a notification for them in this world until the time came, and the word that was a notification was omitted, and it is intended in the speech as it is sufficient to indicate what was mentioned in the speech regarding it. The other is that its meaning is: this Qur’an and the reminder are a notification for them and are sufficient, if they think and consider and remember. And His statement, Then do none destroy except the wicked people? God Almighty says: Then does God destroy with His punishment, when He sends it, anyone except the people who disobeyed His command, rebelled against His obedience, and disbelieved in Him? The meaning of the statement is: God does not destroy anyone except the wicked people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Then are none destroyed except the wicked people? Learn that none is destroyed by God except one who has turned his back on Islam, or a hypocrite who speaks the truth with his tongue but contradicts it with his actions. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Any servant of my nation who intends to do a good deed, one good deed will be recorded for him, and if he does it, ten times as much will be recorded for him. Any servant of my nation who intends to do a bad deed, but it is not recorded for him, but if he does it, one bad deed will be recorded for him, and then it will follow, and God will erase it, and none will perish except one who is perishing.”
